newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - EU has doubts over P&O/Stena ferry link.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - EU has doubts over P&O/Stena ferry link.

text.p: The European Commission is concerned that a proposed joint venture between Britain's P&O and Sweden's Stena Line could stifle competition in operations across the English Channel, EU sources said on Thursday.
The Commission's competition service has drafted a "letter of serious doubts" about the deal, which would merge the two companies' Channel ferry operations.

A final decision on whether to send the letter will be taken by Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert in consultation with Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock and the Commission's legal service. But the sources said it was likely to be sent.
Van Miert usually follows his services' advice.
Sources said the problem with the deal was that it could divide the cross-Channel market between the joint venture and Le Shuttle, the car-train service through the Channel Tunnel.
"The major fear...is the risk of a duopoly situation between Le Shuttle and this outfit," one source said.

P&O, the Peninsular and Orient Navigation Company, and Stena plan to merge operations across the Channel, notably on the lucrative Dover-Calais route where they will run services approximately every 45 minutes.
The deal is also under investigation by British competition authorities. One EU source said the British had similar concerns but he noted that EU law took precedence no matter the findings in London.
P&O said in London it was "still confident" its proposed joint venture with Stena would go ahead. "We are not expecting any major delay," a P&O spokesman told Reuters.
Stena's senior vice president for finance Anders Hedberg, told reporters in Brussels it would be a major surprise if the European Union executive rejected the deal.
But, he said, he expected that the Commission would ask for changes in the deal.

"We are talking (about) a theoretical thing now, but of course we realise that a possible okay from the authorities could mean that we also have to...meet up to certain conditions which is quite common in competition cases," he said.
The Commission has until next Wednesday to raise any objections or the planned link-up between the two companies will get an automatic six-year exemption from EU competition rules.
The EU sources played down the announcement earlier this week by Stena that the French authorities, which are also investigating the deal, had given the green light.
"What the French said was we let this go, but we will be watching this carefully in a number of points," one source said.
There is no deadline for the Commission to come to a final ruling if the EU investigation goes beyond next week.
